prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP Manifesto 2010 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core stance:
- Leave the European Union to restore UK sovereignty, control borders, lawmaking, trade, and budgets. Assert that EU membership imposes heavy costs, regulation and judicial overreach. Call for a referendum on EU membership and wider use of binding national/local referenda.

Economy, tax, regulation:
- Simplify and cut taxes: raise personal allowance to £11,500; introduce a 31% flat tax merging income tax and employee NI; phase out employers’ NI over five years; abolish Inheritance Tax when affordable; stop penalising couples.
- Replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax, channel more business rates to councils; cut council tax by scrapping EU-driven costs and “non-jobs”.
- Reduce public sector to 1997 size; cut quangos; protect frontline services while eliminating waste.
- Scrap up to 120,000 EU directives; restore UK control of financial regulation; return bank oversight to the Bank of England; separate retail and investment banking (Glass–Steagall style); raise capital ratios; reintroduce a lending “corset”.

Jobs, enterprise, skills:
- Create c.1m skilled jobs via long-term programmes: defence re-equipment, nuclear build-out, flood/coastal defences, transport upgrades, prison construction.
- Establish Production Enterprise Centres to support SMEs.
- Denationalise universities/FE with universal Student/Training Vouchers; institutions become independent charities.
- Protect strategic firms from foreign takeovers; scrap EU climate/landfill costs on business.

Immigration and asylum:
- Five-year freeze on permanent immigration; aim to cap future settlement to ≤50,000 p.a.; leave the EU to regain border control; time-limited work permits and visas; criminalise overstaying; triple border staff.
- Points-based system after freeze; deport illegal residents; no amnesties; restore “Primary Purpose Rule”.
- Repeal the Human Rights Act; withdraw from ECHR; restrict asylum to first safe country; use secure centres; limit appeals; require visas and health insurance (with exceptions).
- End state promotion of multiculturalism.

Law and order:
- Elected County Police Boards; return to visible policing.
- Scrap HRA; “life means life”; double prison places; end early release; three-strikes policy; strengthen home defence rights; withdraw from European Arrest Warrant; abolish CPS in favour of local prosecutions; youth “boot camps”.

Defence:
- Increase defence spending by 40%; expand Army and TA; rebuild Navy with carriers; more RAF lift/rotary and JSF; maintain and later replace Trident; prioritise NATO; review Afghanistan; cut MOD bureaucracy; improve forces’ pay and care.

Health:
- No frontline cuts; elected County Health Boards; abolish SHAs/PCTs; franchise services to charitable/not-for-profit/private operators under fixed budgets; health vouchers to opt out; restore matrons, on-the-job nurse training; free eye tests and dental check-ups.

Education:
- School vouchers; retain/expand grammars and create “professional schools”; comprehensive merit testing; more in-school teacher training; drop 50% HE target; restore academic selection by universities; student grants via vouchers; elected County Education Boards; franchise schools; strengthen discipline; support special schools and home education.

Pensions and welfare:
- Citizens’ Pension of at least £130/week, non-means-tested; reinstate dividend tax credit; freeze unaffordable public sector pensions; simplify benefits into a Basic Cash Benefit; enhance Child Benefit and Nursery Vouchers; benefits limited to citizens/residents ≥5 years; introduce workfare.

Trade, foreign affairs:
- Leave political EU; pursue WTO seat; seek Commonwealth Free Trade Area; global trade deals; promote democracy abroad.

Energy, environment, transport, housing:
- Provide up to 50% electricity from nuclear; support domestic coal; oppose most onshore wind; repeal Climate Change Act and EU climate schemes; commission on climate science.
- Invest £3bn p.a. in transport; new bypasses; fuel duty “windfall return”; three high-speed rail lines; Britdisc for foreign lorries; oppose Heathrow expansion in favour of a Thames Estuary hub.
- Control immigration to reduce housing demand; reuse empty homes; scrap regional planning bodies and HIPs; local referenda on major developments; protect Green Belt via elected conservators.

Constitution and culture:
- Direct democracy (5% trigger for referenda); AV+ electoral reform; elected local Boards; devolved business handled by national MPs; right of recall; abolish regional government; support monarchy; Parliament to ratify treaties/war.
- Civic nationalism; oppose multiculturalism; protect British measures, Post Office; UK company/brand register; English Parliament; new public holidays; measures against extremist Islam including limited burqa/niqab bans.

Rural, fishing, other:
- Leave CFP; reclaim 200nm EEZ; ban discards/industrial trawling; rebuild fleet.
- Support farmers via labelling, co-ops, supermarket ombudsman; cautious GM stance.
- Support Post Office/Royal Mail; designated smoking rooms in pubs; prioritise small businesses.
